result:
Solution 1 identifies q* with the upper critical exponent (N+α)/(N−2). That is the end of the allowed range for q, so it cannot be a threshold inside the interval. Its argument is also only heuristic.

Solutions 2 and 3 both derive the mass-critical exponent (N+α+2)/N, and the two expressions are the same number. I did not derive the threshold myself. I believe it matches a known result on Choquard equations with the lower critical exponent, but I am recalling that from memory and have not confirmed it. The scaling argument in both solutions is only a heuristic for the threshold. The one check I did was that (N+α+2)/N lies inside the admissible range, because (N+α+2)(N−2) < N(N+α) reduces to −2α−4 < 0.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
